name: CoDesign and Participatory Futures
description:
This course examines how design shapes development through participation, production systems, and institutional infrastructures. It introduces critical frameworks on dependency, modern design, wicked problems, and India’s design–development discourse. 
Students conduct limited field engagement (3–4 visits), run a co-design session, and translate evidence into an intervention (product/service/scheme/toolkit) with an enabling layer (training/manual/governance/spares/rollout). 
Two studio seminars cover literature and fieldwork. A group paper (Methods–Findings–Intervention–Evaluation) begins at the mid-point.
